title: Coding

1.label: below
1.name: Below the bar
1.meaning: Concerning for this level; this alone would likely block an offer.

2.label: developing
2.name: Developing
2.meaning: Some signal, but clear gaps for this level.

3.label: meets_bar
3.name: Meets the bar
3.meaning: What a solid candidate at the chosen level shows.

4.label: above_bar
4.name: Above the bar
4.meaning: Would read as the next level up.

level_bar.junior: Easy to medium problem. Reaches a working approach with some guidance; correct complexity once asked; tests at least the happy path and one edge case.
level_bar.mid: Medium problem. Drives to an optimal or near optimal approach with at most a level two hint; clean structure; names edge cases and traces one.
level_bar.senior: Medium to hard problem. States the optimal approach within about five minutes, compares it with an alternative, codes it cleanly by about ten minutes, tests unprompted and handles the twist.
level_bar.staff: Same bar as senior on the problem, plus crisp reasoning about trade-offs in the twist (memory, streaming, concurrency) and how the code would hold up in production.

competencies.name: Problem understanding
competencies.looks_for: Clarifying questions on inputs, limits and edge cases before coding; stating assumptions; narrating choices while working.

descriptors.1: Starts without clarifying anything; long silences or half thoughts that are dropped without a reason.
descriptors.2: Asks one or two questions; narration is patchy and some decisions go unexplained.
descriptors.3: Clarifies inputs and edge cases up front; explains each choice as it is made.
descriptors.4: Drives the conversation: states assumptions, checks them with the interviewer, and summarises the plan before coding.

competencies.name: Problem solving
competencies.looks_for: Reaching a correct and efficient approach, correct time and space cost, comparing alternatives, and how much hinting was needed.

descriptors.1: No workable approach, even after hints, or defends a clearly wrong complexity after a counter example.
descriptors.2: Brute force only, or reaches the optimal approach only after level three or higher hints; complexity partly wrong.
descriptors.3: Reaches the optimal approach with at most a level two hint; time and space stated correctly.
descriptors.4: Compares two or more approaches, reaches the optimal one unaided, and handles the twist with a sound idea.

competencies.name: Implementation
competencies.looks_for: Dictated code or ordered blocks that match the approach, with sound control flow and edge handling. Syntax and typing are not assessed.

descriptors.1: Cannot express or order the solution.
descriptors.2: Code or ordering works only with notable gaps or logic bugs; drifts from the stated approach.
descriptors.3: Correct, clean structure that matches the approach; minor slips only.
descriptors.4: Clean and idiomatic, with edge cases handled the first time; decoy lines rejected with a reason.

competencies.name: Testing
competencies.looks_for: Checking the solution: tracing an example, naming edge cases, finding and fixing their own bugs.

descriptors.1: No testing at all, or declares it done with an obvious bug.
descriptors.2: Tests the happy path, and only when asked.
descriptors.3: Traces an example, names relevant edge cases, and finds at least one own bug or confirms none with a trace.
descriptors.4: Tests systematically without being asked and fixes bugs before the interviewer points at them.

scoring_notes: Hints: a level one prompt has no effect; level two costs a little; level three costs more; level four, given only with under about 40 percent of the phase left, costs a lot; a level five give away caps Problem solving at 2.
Ignoring a hint and continuing down a path it ruled out costs more than the hint itself.
Short rounds use ordered solution lines instead of dictated code; judge Implementation from the order, decoys rejected, and the dry run.
Never penalise syntax, language choice, or speech recognition errors in dictated code.
Red flags are only the items in red_flags. Weak, wrong or incomplete answers lower the matching competency score and are never red flags.
red_flags: Makes up facts and keeps defending them after being questioned
Claims to have traced or tested something they never did, and defends it
Hostile, insulting or disrespectful toward the interviewer
Refuses to engage with the questions
Integrity issue, such as reading answers from another source or getting outside help during the round
